## Blockers

### B1 — `design-context.md` still asserts a Mutation Service projection that the shipped implementation and this packet's own type test prove absent

**Files:** `docs/v4/implementation/beta06/design-context.md`, `packages/compiler/src/generate.ts`, `tests/type/beta06-generated-mutation-context.test.ts`, `docs/v4/prototypes/p6-postcommit-outcome/check.ts`

The accepted implementation decision record still says:

> "The generated Mutation Service projection contains only the transitive `read` Service subgraph. An external-effect Service is absent at type level and is also rejected defensively when Runtime bindings are verified."

The **second** sentence is now true and repaired: `validateRuntimeExecutableBindings` gained

```ts
binding.kind === "mutation" && Object.hasOwn(binding.definition, "services")
  → throw new TypeError("Mutation executable binding exposes Services")
```

with a driving hostile case (`beta05-runtime-application.test.ts` "rejects a forged Mutation Service capability before readiness") and a type negative (`ctx.services` under `@ts-expect-error`). That closes the half of the prior B1 that repair option (a) named.

The **first** sentence remains false and is now actively contradicted by the packet:

- `generate.ts` emits `export interface MutationContext extends Omit<RootExecution, "services">`. There is no Service member at all — not a `read` subgraph, not an empty one. `createPostgresMutationInvoker` assembles `ctx` from `{principal, authority, tenant, values, signal, deadline, data, operationTime, callId, transactionId, dispatch}` and never constructs Services.
- `tests/type/beta06-generated-mutation-context.test.ts` commits the opposite claim as a gate: `// @ts-expect-error BETA-06 Mutation Context exposes no Service capability` / `ctx.services;`.

So a byte-pinned decision record advertises a capability seam that a committed compile-time test proves cannot exist. The implementation is strictly safer than the record, but the record is the artifact BETA-07/BETA-08 will read as authority for what a Mutation handler may reach.

**Required repair:** correct the first sentence of `design-context.md` to describe the actual absent-by-construction Service seam (no Service projection on `MutationContext`, external effects deferred to a later Action), and re-pin the byte-compared projection. Note the mechanical coupling: `docs/v4/prototypes/p6-postcommit-outcome/check.ts` lists `docs/v4/implementation/beta06/design-context.md` in `allowedProjectionPaths` and enforces `git diff --quiet <projectionReapplication> HEAD -- <allowedProjectionPaths>`, so the edit must be accompanied by a re-pinned reapplication commit or that check will fail.

## Prior blocker verified closed

**B2 (unreachable `unavailable()` deny paths; no candidate-Policy evidence)** — closed. `tests/unit/beta06-runtime-mutation-transaction.test.ts` "rolls back the receipt and every sibling on Field or candidate Policy denial" drives both zero-row branches of `createPostgresCollectionMutationData` through the real invoker for `fieldAuthority` and `candidatePolicy`, asserts the nondisclosing `"Collection operation is unavailable"`, asserts `ROLLBACK`, asserts no pending-intent insert and no `SET outcome = 'committed'`, and asserts the write statement ran only on the candidate-denial branch. With this, all eight named hostile cases from issue #293 now have driving evidence.

## Non-blocking observations

1. **`QUESTPIE_POSTGRES_MAJOR` still has no committed harness.** `tests/integration/postgres/beta06-publish-mutation.test.ts` hard-requires `expect(declared).toMatch(/^(16|17|18)$/)`, and nothing in the diff sets or defaults it. Acceptance criterion 7 and the manifest's tri-major PASS rest entirely on an external runner; an unconfigured `bun run test:postgres -- --scenario beta06` fails for an environment reason rather than a contract reason. It fails closed, so it is safe, but it is not reproducible from the repository alone.

2. **The claimed replacement reviews have no preserved artifact.** `acceptance-manifest.json` records `"parallel replacement Standards and Spec reviews against diff base 6006800b…": PASS`, but only the BLOCKED `claude-initial-review.json` is committed. Sibling proofs in this same diff byte-preserve their raw reviews (`p6-postcommit-outcome/REVIEW.json`, `REVIEW-02.json`, `beta06-authority-reconciliation/REVIEW.json`). Preserving only the failing review while asserting an unrecorded PASS is an asymmetric evidence record.

3. **Benchmark figure in the manifest is a fourth unlisted observation.** `acceptance-manifest.json` cites `execute20 166.395275 ms`; `quality/baselines/beta06-mutation-transaction.json` records samples `[148.996, 200.795, 216.218]` with `observed: 200.795`. The derivation checks out (`ceil(200.795 × 5 / 100) × 100 = 1100`) and every value is under budget, but the manifest number is not one of the recorded samples.

4. **Production wire-v2 `compatibility` still diverges from the ADR-0023-proved prototype shape.** `packages/compiler/src/runtime/index.ts` emits `wireV1QueryExecution: "allowed"` and no `retainedV1ResultCompatibility`, while `docs/v4/prototypes/p6-postcommit-outcome/wire-v2.json` pins `"allowedWhenCurrentOrRetainedPair"` and `retainedV1ResultCompatibility: "queryOnly"` — the exact key the P6R1 review demanded as its B3 repair. The Mutation-only narrowing is correct in behavior (`application/index.ts` rejects a retained-pair Mutation with `CLIENT_OUTDATED` before Context Resolution, covered by two tests), but it exists only imperatively; the declarative pin cannot catch a regression.

5. **`committedMutation` is sticky per execution root, and the guards are unbraced.** In `packages/runtime/src/application/index.ts` it is set once and never cleared, so a later Query in the same root will not report deadline expiry or cancellation after any committed Mutation. The replay/idempotency path also returns `{committed: true}` despite performing no writes, so a cancelled replay is reported as committed. The nested `if (controlled.deadlineExpired) if (!committedMutation) throw …` chains sit exactly on the ADR-0011 "never claim rollback after commit" boundary and would read more safely with braces or a combined condition.

6. **`xmin` vs `xid8` comparison is epoch-fragile.** `atomicBundle` compares `message.xmin::text` and `event.xmin::text` (32-bit `xid`) against `receipt.transaction_id::text` (`xid8` from `pg_current_xact_id()`). These agree only while the transaction-id epoch is 0 — correct on a fresh test database, not a durable identity assertion.

7. **`retainedClients` remains unreachable from a generated application.** `createRuntimeApplication` accepts it, but the compiler-rendered `internal/application.js` never passes it. Only the synthesized `currentV1` sibling pair can execute a retained v1 Query in a real deployment; the arbitrary-retained-pair path is exercised only in `beta05-runtime-application.test.ts`.

8. **`quality/format-baseline.txt` drops `docs/v4/schema-lifecycle.md` without a corresponding formatting change in this diff.** The replacement entries (the four raw review JSONs) are justified, but the removal is unexplained by the diff; if the exemption was genuinely stale, that is fine, and if not, `quality:release` would have caught it.
